{{Short description|Concept in geometry}}
{{for|the large airplane built by Hughes|Spruce goose}}
In mathematics, a '''Hughes plane''' is one of the [[non-Desarguesian projective plane]]s found by {{harvtxt|Hughes|1957}}.
There are examples of order ''p''<sup>2''n''</sup> for every odd prime ''p'' and every positive integer ''n''.

==Construction==
The construction of a Hughes plane is based on a [[Near-field (mathematics)|nearfield]] '''N''' of order ''p''<sup>''2n''</sup> for ''p'' an odd prime whose kernel '''K''' has order ''p''<sup>''n''</sup> and coincides with the center of '''N'''.

==Properties==
A Hughes plane '''H''':<ref>{{harvnb|Dembowski|1968|loc=pg.247}}</ref>
# is a non-Desarguesian projective plane of odd square prime power order of Lenz-Barlotti type I.1,
# has a Desarguesian Baer subplane '''H'''<sub>0</sub>,
# is a self-dual plane in which every orthogonal polarity of '''H'''<sub>0</sub> can be extended to a polarity of '''H''',
# every central collineation of '''H'''<sub>0</sub> extends to a central collineation of '''H''', and
# the full collineation group of '''H''' has two point orbits (one of which is '''H'''<sub>0</sub>), two line orbits, and four flag orbits.

==The smallest Hughes Plane (order 9)==
The Hughes plane of order 9 was actually found earlier by Veblen and Wedderburn in 1907.<ref>{{Citation|last1=Veblen|first1=O.|last2=Wedderburn|first2=J.H.M.|title=Non-Desarguesian and non-Pascalian geometries|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|year=1907|volume=8|issue=3|pages=379–388|doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-1907-1500792-1|url=https://zenodo.org/record/1431565/files/article.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref> A construction of this plane can be found in {{harvtxt|Room|Kirkpatrick|1971}} where it is called the plane Ψ.
